<!-- pr-reviewer: 58c156e34cb67ef3b80c83366411593de3cc6d5f -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (merge order: after its parent #957, see note).

**What looks good**
- Draw-what-is-judged holds. `operation::turning_holder::body_axes` (turning_holder.rs:78-87) runs the same `Frame::about` and `SignedMeridian::of` that `judge` uses (turning_holder.rs:~109-117). The drawn pose `tip + x*radial + y*(z x x) + z*along` therefore uses the holder law's own X (signed radial, so OD vs ID handedness follows the path) and Z (spindle). The facets are the same `ToolBody::facets` mesh the `LatheClearance` is derived from, so nothing is revolved or approximated.
- Missing or degenerate cases do not panic. No lathe body: `Ok(None)` and the current drawing (axis marker) is kept. No source, no spindle fit, or zero/non-finite/skew frame: a named refusal, logged once, nothing drawn, no guessed pose (`LatheAxes::new`, sim_lathe_body.rs:42-48; `SimToolCache::refuse`). No unwrap/expect/panic in the new module.
- Display only: no verdict, warning or posted output changes. The ui seam (`world::sim_tool_tris`) is unchanged; only a doc comment moved. No snapshot PNGs, no build.rs/.github/scripts/Cargo changes, no process files.
- Pinning tests check vertex by vertex against the law's radius identity for both OD (shank out and up) and ID (bar toward the axis, up the bore), plus cache reuse/rebuild/free-on-clear and refusal of bad frames. Files stay under 400 lines (sim_tool_body.rs 291, sim_lathe_body.rs 153). Provenance line present. Decision file `docs/decisions/1038-lathe-body-in-sim.md` present.

**Local results** (trial merge with upstream/main is clean; no conflicts)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| app: sim_lathe_body 5, sim_tool_body 7, tool_body 12, tool_body_bands 13, tool_body_judged 8, tool_cutter_profile 5, tool_neck_laws 4, tool_spun_profile 7, turning_holder 8, turning_insert_zone 5 | all pass |
| app: lathe_field_sim, lathe_spindle_law, solid_law | pass |
| tools lib 62, sim lib 70 + fixture_stack_span, midmove_pose, overhang_laws, fixture_mesh | pass |
| motion solid_law | pass |
| ui lib (`--test-threads=1`, cwd crates/ui) | 531 passed, 5 ignored |
| clippy `-D warnings` (app, ui, sim, tools, all targets) | clean |

(`cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` printed the whole workspace plan on the merged tree, so I ran the touched and gate-mapped suites by hand instead of the whole plan.)

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. Stacked on #957: this PR's diff includes #957's commit (neck envelope, tools/sim changes). Per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack", retarget this to main before merging #957 (so `--delete-branch` does not close it), then merge #957 first.
2. As the body says, no one has stepped a turning op in the live GUI; the tests assert the pose against the law numerically, which is the stronger guarantee for handedness, but a quick eyeball of an ID bore in the viewport would be a good smoke check. Tinting on `HolderHit` is rightly left out.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
